correctness.rationale: All path candidates between theta vertices are classified by the common poles. For each arm-internal pair, direct and alternative path lengths yield the exact tie/strict-detour counts; for b-c cross pairs the four simple routes reduce to two affine groups and the two duplicate-minimum boundaries are counted explicitly. Pole pairs and shortest-arm cross pairs complete a disjoint partition. The resulting formula was independently checked against BFS shortest-path counts on 364 complete parameter triples and 200 reproducible wider triples. Finite evidence is corroboration, not the universal proof. Exact quantifiers require integer lengths at least 2.

originality.rationale: The new theorem gives an all-parameter constant-time closed parity formula for the complete geodesic subpath number of exactly three internally disjoint paths of arbitrary lengths. The complete accessible text of Knor et al. (2026) supplies formulas for grids, hypercubes and layered joins and cactus extremal theorems, but does not compute this noncactus theta family. The relevant research records  concern other invariants or other graph families. Searches yielded no implication-equivalent or dominating formula; historical priority remains provisional, and this absence of retrieval is not treated as a proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The gpn invariant was recently studied on cacti and selected product families. Three-path theta graphs are the canonical first overlapping-cycle 2-connected series-parallel family, where two route groups and a third-arm shortcut create noncactus tie phenomena, including triple geodesics. A fixed-size exact formula for all three independent arm lengths is a natural complete family answer, usable for extremal exploration without claiming a general graph theorem. This is not merely a substitution of existing cactus formulas.
